principles: hashed bundles are immutable: cache them at the edge
the SPA shell names the bundles: never cache it
authenticated API traffic and live streams pass through untouched: a shared cache must never hold a tenant's bytes

rules.note: Vite content-hashes every bundle name: a changed byte is a new URL, so a year of edge caching is safe — the origin serves 30d/immutable and the edge must not shorten it below the origin's max-age
the shell is the only unhashed file and it names the hashed ones — a cached shell points at bundles that no longer exist
SPA fallback and static pages follow the shell rule: no shared-cache copies of anything unhashed
authenticated, tenant-scoped bytes: the API's own conditional-get layer (ETag/304, private/no-cache) is the only cache these responses may ever meet
SSE streams never end: buffering one deadlocks the client
